skill.name: python-performance-optimization
skill.description: Profile Python applications, identify CPU and memory bottlenecks, and apply targeted optimization patterns for faster, leaner code.
skill.summary: Use profiling tools and proven Python patterns to find bottlenecks and improve runtime, memory, database, and I/O performance.
skill.author: ActiveInferenceInstitute

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and educational Python examples. The only confirmed issue is low-severity guidance for py-spy commands that attach to live processes and may expose stack traces if used without authorization. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: py-spy examples attach to a running process by PID.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short warning to use py-spy only on systems and processes where the user has authorization, because stack traces may expose sensitive details.

remediation.issue: HTTP benchmark examples call an external demonstration service.
remediation.suggestion: Mention that users may replace httpbin.org with a local test endpoint when they cannot make external network requests.

content.value_statement: Slow Python code is hard to improve without clear measurements. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through profiling, benchmarking, and targeted optimization patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use CPU, memory, line, and call graph profiling.
Provides cProfile, pstats, line_profiler, memory_profiler, and py-spy workflows.
Shows benchmark patterns for lists, generators, strings, dictionaries, caching, and function calls.
Covers multiprocessing for CPU-bound work and async I/O for network-bound work.
Includes database, memory leak, iterator, weak reference, and pytest-benchmark examples.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples; it does not run profilers by itself.
Benchmark results depend on hardware, workload size, Python version, and environment.
Some examples require optional packages such as NumPy, py-spy, aiohttp, or pytest-benchmark.
Production profiling needs authorization and care because process data may be sensitive.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a slow service endpoint
use_cases.description: Use profiling output to identify hot functions, expensive queries, or blocking I/O before changing code.

use_cases.title: Reduce memory pressure in data jobs
use_cases.description: Compare list-based processing with generators, iterators, weak references, and memory profiling techniques.

use_cases.title: Prepare a performance improvement plan
use_cases.description: Benchmark current behavior, choose focused optimization patterns, and measure results after each change.

prompt_templates.title: Find my first bottleneck
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-performance-optimization skill to help me profile this Python function. Explain which profiler to use first and what result would prove the bottleneck.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a slow loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-performance-optimization skill to review this slow Python loop. Suggest faster data structures or built-in operations, then explain how to benchmark the change.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce memory usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-performance-optimization skill to analyze this memory-heavy Python workflow. Identify where generators, iterators, or weak references may reduce memory use.

prompt_templates.title: Build a complete optimization plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-performance-optimization skill to create a measurement-driven optimization plan for this Python application. Include CPU profiling, memory profiling, I/O review, database checks, and benchmark validation.

output_examples.input: My Python batch job is slow, and I do not know where to start.
output: Start with cProfile to find the functions with the highest cumulative time.
Use pstats to sort the results and focus on the top hot paths.
Benchmark one change at a time so each improvement has measured evidence.

output_examples.input: A file-processing script uses too much memory.
output: Check whether the script loads full files or large lists into memory.
Replace full materialization with iterators or generators where possible.
Use memory profiling before and after the change to confirm lower peak usage.

output_examples.input: My API waits on several HTTP calls.
output: Classify the workload as I/O-bound before adding multiprocessing.
Consider async I/O when requests can run concurrently.
Measure latency and error behavior against a safe test endpoint.

best_practices: Profile before optimizing so changes target measured bottlenecks.
Keep benchmarks small, repeatable, and close to the real workload.
Compare before and after results, including runtime, memory, and correctness.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize code paths that are not part of the measured slowdown.
Do not assume a microbenchmark result applies to every production workload.
Do not attach profilers to production processes without authorization.

faq.question: Does this skill execute profilers automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, and command patterns that the user can choose to run.

faq.question: Which profiler should I start with?
faq.answer: Start with cProfile for CPU time, then use memory_profiler or tracemalloc when memory is the suspected bottleneck.

faq.question: Can it help with production performance issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses py-spy for live profiling, but users should only profile authorized systems and processes.

faq.question: Does it cover database performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes batch inserts, query planning, indexes, and selecting only needed columns.

faq.question: Can it help with network-bound Python code?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares synchronous requests with async I/O for workloads that wait on external services.

faq.question: Will every optimization improve my application?
faq.answer: No. The skill emphasizes measuring before and after because results depend on workload, data size, and runtime environment.
